gloss: to be nervous; to be apprehensive; to be jumpy

definitions.gloss: to be nervous; to be apprehensive; to be on edge
definitions.explanation: Describes a state of constant nervousness or apprehension, where someone is anxiously anticipating something bad happening. Often implies living in fear of a specific threat or authority.

examples.japanese: びくびくしないで⟦{堂々|どうどう}→堂々：05895_doudou⟧とし⟦なさい→なさる：01307_nasaru⟧。
examples.english: Don't be so nervous — stand tall.

examples.japanese: ⟦{上司|じょうし}→上司：03286_joushi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{顔色|かおいろ}→顔色：25468_kaoiro⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧びくびくし⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧{窺|うかが}って⟦いた→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: I was nervously watching my boss's expression.

examples.japanese: ⟦{秘密|ひみつ}→秘密：02504_himitsu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ばれる→ばれる：06721_bareru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ではないか→ではないか：30627_dehanaika⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{毎日|まいにち}→毎日：00729_mainichi⟧びくびくして⟦{暮|く}らしていた→暮らす：01937_kurasu⟧。
examples.english: I lived every day in fear that my secret would be discovered.

notes:
An onomatopoeic word describing a state of constant nervousness or fear. Unlike a momentary startle, ⟦びくびく→びくびく：05266_bikubiku⟧ implies an ongoing, sustained state of anxiety — being jumpy or on edge over a period of time.

FORMS:
- びくびくする: verb form
- びくびくし⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧: while being nervous
- びくびくして⟦{暮|く}らす→暮らす：01937_kurasu⟧: to live in fear

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- びくびくして⟦{暮|く}らす→暮らす：01937_kurasu⟧: to live nervously, to live in constant fear
- びくびくし⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧⟦{待|ま}つ→待つ：00469_matsu⟧: to wait nervously
- ⟦びくびく→びくびく：05266_bikubiku⟧もの: something nerve-wracking (colloquial)

RELATED WORD びくっとする:
びくっ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ describes a single, sudden startle reaction (a flinch or jolt), while びくびくする is the ongoing state of being on edge.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦おどおどする→おどおどする：21631_odoodosuru⟧: to be timid — focuses on visible timidity and lack of confidence rather than fear
- ⟦ハラハラする→ハラハラする：16932_haraharasuru⟧: to be anxious — often used when watching someone else in a tense situation
- おびえる: to be frightened — a stronger, more direct fear
